protocol.question: When the deployed Boolean CBM explains a prediction with a small set of concepts: are the concepts sufficient for its decision (logical sufficiency, independently verified) and correct for the image (premise support vs CUB image-level annotations)?
protocol.main_output: P(correct prediction AND verified sufficient reason AND all premises annotation-supported), with components reported separately
protocol.frozen_pipeline: DINOv3 cached features, oracle GT part boxes, concept readers on pooled region features (val-carved), CART T depth12 on labels / mean-patch linear teacher + distilled CART D depth4
protocol.cbm_head: multinomial logistic on continuous concept scores
protocol.cem_head: per-part trunk 384-128-16, concept embeddings -> linear task head, aux concept heads, CE+BCE joint; NOT certified (embeddings may encode beyond concept labels; exact certificates reserved for the deployed Boolean model)
protocol.premise_trichotomy: literal supported/refuted vs annotation; literals over unobserved parts flagged unresolved (reader never read the region)
protocol.selectors: default min-size / confidence max calibrated q / annotation-oracle max supported; exact exhaustive over <=2^12 path-literal subsets
prereg_readouts: A2 P(all supported) < accuracy at every K>=4
A5 unresolved literals occur in reasons
